title: Seven In 10 Americans Expect AI To Cost Jobs, Pew Finds
key_facts: Pew found 71% of Americans expect AI to lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years; 5% expect more, 10% no difference.
Only Australia and South Korea (76% each) were higher among 37 countries; the median was 46%.
The US figure is up 7 points from 64% in August 2024.
52% of Americans say more AI in daily life makes them more concerned than excited; 9% more excited.
Among 18 to 34 year olds, 55% are more concerned than excited, up from 40% in 2024.
46% say AI will widen the gap between rich and poor.
US surveys: 3,488 adults (June 22-28) and 5,119 adults (Feb 17-23); international: 42,151 adults in 36 other countries.
quote_evidence: Pew Research Center found that 71% of Americans expect AI to lead to fewer jobs in the country over the next 20 years, while 5% expect more jobs and 10% expect no difference.
The US figure is up 7 points from 64% in August 2024, and the US is the only country where Pew has asked the question before.
why_it_matters_hint: Public worry about AI and jobs is rising, especially among the young.
event_date: Surveys Feb to Jun 2026 (international Feb 8 to May 13)
notes: Survey of opinion, not a measure of actual job losses. Radio Ink relays Pew.
